key_insight: Simulation-based reinforcement learning improved a language model’s psychiatric intake performance, outperforming its base model in 76.7% of matched role-play scenario pairs.
clinical_relevance: The findings suggest potential for clinician-supervised psychiatric intake support, but do not establish safety or effectiveness in real patient care.
method: Trained a language model through multi-turn reinforcement learning in simulated psychiatric intake environments.
Compared trained and identically prompted base models in a randomized, double-blind crossover study with psychiatrist-enacted patients.
Stress-tested conversational safety using 256 adversarial presentations derived from Delphi-consensus taxonomies.
evidence_signal: Across 60 matched scenario pairs (120 encounters), 32 psychiatrists role-played patients and 15 independent psychiatrists scored transcripts; the trained model’s win rate was 76.7% (p < 0.0001).
watch_item: Evaluation used simulated and psychiatrist-enacted encounters, and acute-risk under-triage persisted at 12.9% in adversarial testing, underscoring the need for safeguards and clinician oversight.
paper_title: Training language models in simulation for psychiatric intake
